source_metadata.title: Perioperative Bridging Anticoagulation in Patients with Atrial Fibrillation
source_metadata.source_boundary: Primary-study atoms were derived from the primary article; supplement-derived eligibility/outcome definitions are explicitly anchored to the Supplementary Appendix. The protocol was used as supporting prespecification context and not treated as a separate study.

atoms.canonical_statement: The BRIDGE trial tested whether forgoing perioperative heparin bridging during temporary warfarin interruption was noninferior to dalteparin bridging for preventing arterial thromboembolism and superior for major bleeding.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We hypothesized that forgoing bridging anticoagulation would be noninferior ... and would be superior ... with respect to major bleeding.

atoms.canonical_statement: BRIDGE was a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial conducted at 108 sites in the United States and Canada.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The BRIDGE trial was a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial.

atoms.canonical_statement: The trial randomized 1,884 patients; mean age was 71.7 years, 73.4% were male, and mean CHADS2 score was 2.3.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: we recruited 1884 patients ... The mean age ... 71.7 years ... 73.4% ... male ... mean CHADS2 score ... 2.3

population.label: Adults with chronic atrial fibrillation or flutter receiving warfarin who required interruption for an elective procedure

atoms.canonical_statement: Eligible participants were adults receiving warfarin for at least 3 months with target INR 2.0-3.0, requiring temporary interruption for an elective procedure, with chronic atrial fibrillation/flutter and at least one major CHADS2 stroke-risk factor.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: All of the following 5 criteria must be satisfied for trial eligibility

population.label: Trial-eligible adults
inclusion_criteria: At least one major stroke risk factor

atoms.canonical_statement: Key exclusions included mechanical prosthetic heart valves, stroke/systemic embolism/TIA or venous thromboembolism within 12 weeks, major bleeding within 6 weeks, creatinine clearance below 30 mL/min, platelets below 100 x 10^9/L, pregnancy, heparin allergy/HIT, and specified high-risk cardiac or intracranial/intraspinal procedures.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: One or more of the following criteria precludes trial eligibility

atoms.canonical_statement: Bridging consisted of dalteparin 100 IU/kg subcutaneously twice daily from 3 days before the procedure until about 24 hours before it, then resumed after the procedure for 5-10 days according to bleeding risk.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: dalteparin sodium (100 IU per kilogram ... subcutaneously twice daily) ... from 3 days before ... until 24 hours before ... and then for 5 to 10 days after

atoms.canonical_statement: The no-bridging strategy used matching subcutaneous placebo during the same perioperative schedule while warfarin was interrupted.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: receive no bridging therapy (i.e., a matching subcutaneous placebo)

atoms.canonical_statement: Warfarin was stopped 5 days before the procedure and restarted on the evening of or the day after the procedure at the usual dose; study drug was resumed 12-24 hours after low-bleeding-risk procedures and 48-72 hours after high-bleeding-risk procedures until INR was at least 2.0 once.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Warfarin treatment was discontinued 5 days before ... restarted ... study drug was restarted 12 to 24 hours ... and 48 to 72 hours ... until the INR was 2.0 or higher

atoms.canonical_statement: The primary efficacy outcome was arterial thromboembolism comprising stroke, transient ischemic attack, or systemic embolism, assessed through 30 days.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The primary efficacy outcome was arterial thromboembolism, including stroke ... transient ischemic attack, and systemic embolism

outcome.definition: Stroke (ischemic or hemorrhagic), transient ischemic attack, or systemic embolism, assessed through 30 days after the procedure.

atoms.canonical_statement: The primary safety outcome was major bleeding; the supplementary appendix defined it using symptomatic/clinically overt ISTH-based criteria including transfusion, hemoglobin decline, intervention, critical-site bleeding, or fatal bleeding.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The primary bleeding endpoint is major bleeding, defined by one or more of the events defined by the International Society on Thrombosis and Haemostasis.

outcome.definition: Symptomatic or clinically overt bleeding meeting ISTH-based criteria including >=2 units transfusion, hemoglobin decrease >2 g/dL, reoperation/invasive intervention, critical-site bleeding, or fatal bleeding.

atoms.canonical_statement: All study outcomes were independently and blindly adjudicated.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: All study outcomes were independently and blindly adjudicated.

atoms.canonical_statement: The primary efficacy analysis used a one-sided noninferiority test with a 1.0-percentage-point margin; noninferiority was concluded if the upper 95% confidence bound for the between-group risk difference was below 1.0 percentage point.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The primary analysis of efficacy was a noninferiority analysis ... noninferiority margin was set at 1.0% ... upper boundary ... less than 1.0 percentage point.

atoms.canonical_statement: At 30 days, arterial thromboembolism occurred in 0.4% with no bridging and 0.3% with bridging; the 0.1-percentage-point risk difference (95% CI -0.6 to 0.8) met the prespecified noninferiority criterion.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Arterial thromboembolism 4 (0.4) 3 (0.3)

population.label: Randomized patients with available 30-day outcome data

outcome.definition: Stroke (ischemic or hemorrhagic), transient ischemic attack, or systemic embolism, assessed through 30 days after the procedure.

quantitative_result.effect_measure: risk difference (percentage points; no bridging minus bridging)
quantitative_result.p_value_text: P=0.01 for noninferiority; P=0.73 for superiority
quantitative_result.original_result_text: 0.4% vs 0.3%; risk difference 0.1 percentage points; 95% CI -0.6 to 0.8; P=0.01 for noninferiority

atoms.canonical_statement: Major bleeding occurred in 1.3% with no bridging and 3.2% with bridging; no bridging was superior (RR 0.41, 95% CI 0.20-0.78; P=0.005).

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Major bleeding 12 (1.3) 29 (3.2) 0.005

outcome.definition: Symptomatic or clinically overt bleeding meeting ISTH-based criteria including >=2 units transfusion, hemoglobin decrease >2 g/dL, reoperation/invasive intervention, critical-site bleeding, or fatal bleeding.

atoms.canonical_statement: Minor bleeding was less frequent with no bridging than bridging (12.0% vs 20.9%; P<0.001).

quantitative_result.effect_measure: risk difference (percentage points; no bridging minus bridging)

atoms.canonical_statement: Death occurred in 0.5% of the no-bridging group and 0.4% of the bridging group; the between-group difference was not statistically significant.

atoms.canonical_statement: Among patients who underwent the anticipated procedure, 89.4% underwent procedures classified as minor/low bleeding risk according to the prespecified classification.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Overall, 89.4% of patients underwent a procedure that was classified as minor (low bleeding risk)

atoms.canonical_statement: Mean dalteparin dose among bridging patients was 9,093 IU subcutaneously twice daily; protocol adherence to study-drug dosing was 86.5% before and 96.5% after the procedure.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: mean dose of dalteparin ... 9093±2240 IU ... Adherence ... 86.5% before ... 96.5% after

atoms.canonical_statement: Patients with CHADS2 scores of 5 or 6 were underrepresented, limiting certainty in the highest-stroke-risk atrial-fibrillation patients.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Few patients had a CHADS2 score of 5 or 6

atoms.canonical_statement: Major surgical procedures associated with high rates of arterial thromboembolism and bleeding were not represented, limiting generalizability to those procedures.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Patients undergoing major surgical procedures associated with high rates of arterial thromboembolism and bleeding ... were not represented

atoms.canonical_statement: The findings should not be applied to patients with mechanical heart valves because they were specifically excluded.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: the findings should not be applied to patients with mechanical heart valves

atoms.canonical_statement: The observed arterial thromboembolism rate was lower than expected, and the prespecified 1.0-percentage-point noninferiority margin was large relative to the observed event rate.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: the overall rate of arterial thromboembolism was lower than expected ... the noninferiority margin ... turned out to be large in relation to the actual observed event rate

atoms.canonical_statement: For patients with atrial fibrillation requiring temporary interruption of warfarin for an elective procedure, forgoing bridging was noninferior to dalteparin bridging for arterial thromboembolism prevention and reduced major bleeding.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: a strategy of forgoing bridging anticoagulation was noninferior ... and ... decreased the risk of major bleeding

extraction_limitations: The trial article reports a randomized comparison of bridging versus no bridging; this extraction does not create primary-study atoms from studies cited in the Discussion.
Secondary outcome risk differences were calculated from reported arm percentages and are labeled calculated_from_reported_data.
The supporting protocol is substantially longer than the published article and was used selectively to confirm prespecified design/endpoints; protocol administrative material was not atomized.
